books.title: Tenth Annual Report of the Board of Public Works
books.author: Chicago Board of Public Works
books.date_scope: Fiscal year ending March 31, 1871; commissioners’ letter July 1; p. 17 adds an event on July 15. Individual sections specify their own dates.
books.rights: Public-domain 1871 municipal report; Google-digitized copy available through Internet Archive.
books.bias: Administrative self-report. Expenditure, assessment, proposal, completed work and measured observation are different kinds of evidence.

pages.title: New hydrants: date definition and South Division

records.title: New hydrant — northeast corner Chicago avenue and Pine street
records.historical_location: northeast corner Chicago avenue and Pine street
records.date_scope: Year ending April 1, 1871 (the hydrant section’s own wording).
records.finding: One new hydrant is recorded at this location; p. 79 defines the list as installations in the year ending April 1, 1871.
records.excerpt: One northeast corner Chicago avenue and Pine street.
records.render_use: Add a hydrant candidate with the recorded corner or offset. Resolve curb line and period hydrant design before placement.
records.limitations: The list supplies neither model, height, paint, pressure nor exact curb setback. It is a subset of new installations, not all hydrants in the city.

records.title: Street names appear on city lamps
records.finding: The superintendent praises the recently adopted practice of putting street names on lamps and notes that maintenance can move lamps onto the wrong streets.
records.locator: Street names appear on city lamps
records.excerpt: placing the names of streets upon the lamps of the city
records.render_use: Create a research task for lamp-mounted street labels; distinguish this from a generic modern signpost.
records.limitations: No lettering design, dimensions, complete installation list or evidence of coverage at every corner is supplied.
